item.title: The Mind Blowing Fix for 90 Percent Packet Loss on my PDP-11s
item.description:
My LED sign took down two PDP-11s. Not with a power surge. Not with a bad cable. With a single bit in a MAC address.
Everything looked fine. The sign was playing. The fast switches had bandwidth to spare. The PDP-11s were perfectly responsive at their own consoles. But the moment I tried to use them over the network, 90% of the packets vanished. Telnet sessions became unusable. Both machines — one Unibus, one QBus — started dropping traffic at the same time.
After swapping cables, ports, adapters, and even entire OS installs, I finally noticed the switch was shoving nearly 10 Mbps of multicast frames at machines that only have 10 Mbps half-duplex links. Upstream the traffic was 22 Mbps. Downstream on the PDP ports it was maxing the pipe. The switch had logged tens of millions of transmit drops.
The culprit turned out to be the Colorlight receiver card driving my LED banner. It speaks raw Ethernet (no IP) to a fixed MAC address whose low bit marks it as multicast. The switch flooded those frames everywhere. IGMP snooping couldn’t help because there was no IP multicast group to snoop. The modern LED gear was fine. The vintage NICs were not.
This is the detective story of how I tracked it down (with a little help from ChatGPT reading the UniFi console), why only the PDP-11s suffered, and the clean VLAN fix that let the sign keep running while the old machines got their network back.
If you’ve ever had an old machine suddenly get slow on a modern network, this one’s for you.
Live PDP-11s: [pdp1173.com](https://pdp1173.com/)
Download TMOG Free: https://tmog.org
